transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Anya Patel (Redwood CSM), Sarah Lin (Astra Head of ML), Devon Park (Astra Infra), Tom Hales (Astra CTO)

Auto-summary: Quick review of this week's benchmark artifacts; Redwood shows ~20% better P95 on complex prompts vs baseline provider on same VM spec, throughput tradeoffs depend heavily on batch config and kv-cache hit rates. Next: run live dedicated load test and share logs + security docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we got 45 minutes on the calendar, is this time still good?
[00:06] Sarah: yeah works for me, thanks maya.
[00:10] Carlos: hi all, quick agenda - results recap, configuration differences, tuning suggestions, and next steps.
[00:18] Devon: quick note we are on a deadline for vendor decision end of month so we wanna lock the perf story.
[00:24] Maya: got it, we'll focus on the head-to-head metrics.
[00:30] Carlos: ok throwing up the spreadsheet, so baseline is ExistingCloudProvider with their standard g4-like instances, we mirrored the model weights and used fp16 quantization, Redwood runs were on our tuned kernels and batching policy.
[00:42] Tom: sorry can you repeat the VM/spec parity? i think devon sent something earlier but want to be sure.
[00:47] Carlos: sure, both runs used 8xA10 equivalent (vCPU/ram matched), same seq length distribution from your traffic sample, baseline had batching set to 8, we ran with adaptive batching starting at 4 up to 16.
[01:05] Sarah: curious on this "adaptive" batching - does that increase tail latency?
[01:09] Carlos: good question, we tune for target SLO. In practice p50 improves and p95 often improves because of better packing, p99 sometimes spikes on really long tails if kv cache misses happen.
[01:22] Devon: wait kv what?
[01:24] Carlos: kv cache, we sometimes see it transcribed as kv cash in notes, basically the model key-value cache for multi-turn context - if hits are high throughput and latency both improve.
[01:33] Sarah: got it. ok show me the numbers.
[01:36] Carlos: right - page 2, aggregate results: Redwood P50 = 85ms vs baseline 120ms, P95 = 210ms vs 260ms, P99 = 430ms vs 480ms. Throughput at concurrency 200: Redwood 620 qps, baseline 510 qps. These are median of 5 runs.
[02:00] Tom: that's promising. any differences in tokenization or prompt framing that could skew latency?
[02:05] Carlos: we used your exact prompt sets and tokenization, same model revision. small variance from startup jitter we filter out.
[02:12] Sarah: what about cost? you mentioned a cost per token delta last week.
[02:15] Maya: yes, rough unit economics - because of higher throughput and caching, Redwood pilot estimates 12-18% lower per-token infra cost at your observed workload. We'll send a detailed cost delta in the spreadsheet.
[02:28] Devon: how confident are you about the caching numbers? our traffic has a lot of single-shot requests so hit rate may be low.
[02:35] Carlos: fair point; caching helps more for multi-turn flows. For single-shot you get benefit from kernel optimizations and compilation choices; we saw ~10% p95 improvement even with low cache hit rates.
[02:47] Sarah: any security implications for dedicated vs hosted? we need KMS and audit logs plus SSO.
[02:53] Anya: we support customer-managed KMS and full audit logs for Dedicated/Private. SSO via SAML/OIDC is supported, we'll share SOC 2 and ISO docs.
[03:03] Tom: great, please attach the compliance pack.
[03:07] Maya: will do.
[03:09] Carlos: back to tuning - quantization: baseline used standard int8 dynamic, we tested both int8 and fp16; on your model int8 had slightly lower memory but introduced minor quality variance on certain prompts. We recommend fp16 for pilot stability.
[03:25] Sarah: hmm we care about quality, so fp16 better if quality holds. any examples?
[03:29] Carlos: i can attach a small diff of outputs, there were about 2% of prompts with truncated completion length in int8 runs.
[03:36] Devon: network - are you assuming VPC peering or internet egress for private deployments? egress costs are a big concern for us.
[03:43] Maya: for Dedicated we support VPC peering and private links, egress minimized. for hosted there is standard internet egress unless you use Private deployment.
[03:52] Sarah: timeline question - if we agree to a pilot, how quickly can we stand up dedicated nodes for a live load test?
[03:58] Carlos: we can spin up a dedicated pool within 3-5 business days once we have capacity and contract. For load tests we often provision temporary extra nodes.
[04:08] Tom: ok let's pencil in a live load for July 22.
[04:11] Maya: added.
[04:13] Sarah: any caveats about the benchmark methodology? i see you ran five runs but not warmup configuration details.
[04:19] Carlos: yes we used 2 warmup minutes and discard first run; warmup improved stability. We'll add exact command-line args and raw logs in the spreadsheet.
[04:27] Devon: are there any reliability alerts or failover tests run? we care about graceful degradation.
[04:32] Carlos: we did a simulated node failure; Redwood's smart routing rebalanced to other nodes and p95 increased ~15% momentarily, then recovered. We'll include that trace.
[04:44] Sarah: cool. about benchmarking vs Anthropic/OpenAI, did you compare?
[04:48] Carlos: not directly in this POC; we focused on your current baseline provider for apples-to-apples. We can add one-off tests vs Anthropic if helpful.
[04:56] Tom: client's procurement will ask about contracts and SLA - what's typical?
[05:00] Maya: for Dedicated pilots we offer a short-term pilot addendum with SLAs for uptime and latency tiers; I'll include options.
[05:08] Sarah: ok next steps recap?
[05:10] Maya: recap: Carlos to share benchmark spreadsheet, raw logs, and warmup args by Friday 2026-07-17; Sarah to send canonical prompt list by Sunday 2026-07-18; Redwood to provision dedicated trial and schedule live load test on 2026-07-22; Maya to send pricing and security docs by 2026-07-16.
[05:28] Devon: sounds good. thanks.
[05:30] Tom: thanks everyone.
[05:32] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in slack and email the artifacts. bye.

References:
- Benchmark spreadsheet link: (shared) https://redwood.share/benchmarks/astra-july15
- Security docs: will attach SOC2 and ISO pack in follow-up

End of transcript.
